messages:
ria: audit flagged a new ClusterRole 'cluster-admin-agg-2026' that unexpectedly aggregated several infra ClusterRoles incl. gpu-provisioner perms. @omar can you take a look? :eyes:

omar: on it. can you paste the `kubectl get clusterrole cluster-admin-agg-2026 -o yaml` output (or a snippet)?

ria: ```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: cluster-admin-agg-2026
aggregationRule:
  clusterRoleSelectors:
  - matchLabels:
      rbac.redwood/aggregation: "infra"
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
# aggregated roles include: gpu-provisioner, deploy-controller, k8s-node-proxy
```

leila: that `matchLabels` change landed with the aggregation refactor yesterday, right? could be the culprit.

sasha: yep — important nuance: AggregationRule selects ClusterRoles by label across the whole cluster (cluster-scoped). If any ClusterRole (even third-party or old ones) got the label `rbac.redwood/aggregation=infra` they get pulled into the aggregated role.

omar: confirmed. `kubectl get clusterrole -l rbac.redwood/aggregation=infra -o name` shows `clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/gpu-provisioner` which we definitely didn't intend to be aggregated.

ria: immediate mitigation: remove the label from the offending clusterroles and revoke any bindings that escalated. I'm removing label from `gpu-provisioner` now.

sasha: also check if there are ClusterRoleBindings or ClusterBindings that bind the aggregated clusterrole to a wide-scoped subject. aggregation makes the ClusterRole bigger, bindings determine exposure.

omar: ran: `kubectl label clusterrole gpu-provisioner rbac.redwood/aggregation-` -> label removed. verified with `kubectl describe clusterrole cluster-admin-agg-2026` shows gpu-provisioner no longer aggregated.

ria: audit shows a ClusterRoleBinding `crb-gpu-provisioner` bound to `system:serviceaccount:kube-system:gpu-provisioner-sa` — it was always there, but now the aggregated clusterrole had extra verbs. we've recorded scope of access and no signs of malicious calls.

leila: good. next steps: rotate the SA token for `gpu-provisioner-sa` and check KMS usage for any odd decrypts during the window. I'll take KMS logs.

sasha: we should prevent this class of issue going forward: 
- disallow `rbac.redwood/aggregation` label on ClusterRole resources unless created by infra pipeline (admission policy)
- change the aggregation operator to prefer `aggregation-owner=infra:<id>` and require an annotation `aggregation-approved: "true"`
- add an alert when aggregated clusterroles change size/number of rules (diff)

omar: short-term: rolled backed aggregation operator to previous version (v2.1) to stop further auto-aggregations. Also applied a validating webhook that rejects ClusterRole creations/patches containing `rbac.redwood/aggregation` label unless `aggregation-owner=infra-pipeline` annotation present.

ria: opened INC-2026-045 and added owners: @omar (lead), @leila (audit/KMS), @sasha (fix PR + webhook). I've also kicked off a scan: `kubectl get clusterrole -l rbac.redwood/aggregation=infra -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}\n{end}'` to ensure no other roles are annotated.

deploy-bot: Rolled back role-aggregation-operator to v2.1 (deploy-3178) — rollout completed :white_check_mark:

leila: KMS logs look clean so far, no anomalous decrypts in the window. continuing scan.

ria: thanks team. follow-up actions: PR to tighten aggregation labels, admission policy change, incident postmortem with timeline + recommended guardrails. Will post links in the incident thread. :lock:
